deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a wrapper or cover sheet for a bundle of folios, written in a neat hand that is probably not Riemann's own; it is more likely an editor's or archivist's (e.g. Dedekind or Weber, or the Göttingen library). It reads: 'Abel'sche Functionen. Entwürfe zu der grossen Abhandlung. Durchsucht.' In English: 'Abelian functions. Drafts for the large memoir. Searched through.' The 'grosse Abhandlung' is almost certainly Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 54, 1857). 'Durchsucht' most plausibly records that the drafts were examined, probably by the editors of the Gesammelte Werke (1876, Nachträge 1902), for material worth publishing. The archival annotations are '71 Bl.' (71 Blätter, i.e. the bundle contains 71 leaves) at top right, and '121' with a further mark ('4' or a stray stroke) in the right margin, which is the foliation or shelf numbering. There are no derivations to reconstruct.
